The first stable release of `memfs-kit`, a lightweight in-memory filesystem
built around Go's `io/fs` interfaces.

## Highlights

- Create and populate a filesystem with `New`, `MkdirAll`, and `WriteFile`, then
  use it with standard `fs` helpers, templates, and `http.FileServer`.
- `*FS` implements `fs.FS` and `fs.SubFS`. Regular file handles support seeking
  and positional reads; directory handles implement `fs.ReadDirFile`.
- Writes copy their input, and open handles retain independent content and
  metadata snapshots. Directory entries are sorted and support consistent
  paginated reads.
- Filesystem operations and individual handle methods support concurrent use.
  Subtree views share the same underlying tree.
- `WithOpenHook` can transform regular files or supply content for missing
  paths. Hooks are preserved across subtrees, and directory metadata reflects
  transformed content.
- Correctness fixes cover locking, file ownership, directory iteration, error
  propagation, hook metadata, and references retained by closed handles.
- No third-party Go module dependencies.

## Installation

Requires **Go 1.27.3 or newer**.

```sh
go get github.com/soulteary/memfs-kit@v1.0.0
```

```go
import memfs "github.com/soulteary/memfs-kit"
```

## Migration from soulteary/memfs

Change the import path from `github.com/soulteary/memfs` to
`github.com/soulteary/memfs-kit`. The package name remains `memfs`, and ordinary
`memfs.New()` calls continue to work.

`New` now accepts variadic options. Code assigning it to an exact
`func() *memfs.FS` variable needs a wrapper:

```go
newFS := func() *memfs.FS { return memfs.New() }
```

Review the [documented behavior](https://github.com/soulteary/memfs-kit/blob/v1.0.0/README.md#behavior-and-boundaries),
[hook semantics](https://github.com/soulteary/memfs-kit/blob/v1.0.0/README.md#open-hooks),
and [upstream review](https://github.com/soulteary/memfs-kit/blob/v1.0.0/docs/UPSTREAM_REVIEW.md)
when migrating. Hook callbacks must synchronize their own shared state and
provide stable output when metadata and content are consumed in separate
operations.

## Validation

CI covers Linux, macOS, and Windows, with Linux race detection and bounded path
fuzzing. Formatting, module consistency, and `go vet` checks remain enabled.

The generated release reports record **97.45% statement coverage** and a
**Go Report Card grade of A+ (94.7%)**. See the
[test report](https://github.com/soulteary/memfs-kit/blob/v1.0.0/.github/go-test-report.md)
and [quality report](https://github.com/soulteary/memfs-kit/blob/v1.0.0/.github/goreportcard-report.md).
